summary: Lancelot Wilkinson (1805–1841) was an Indologist who studied at the East India Company College around 1821–1823. He held a post in the Bombay Civil Service in 1822 and taught Bapu Deva Sastri, Subaji Bapu, and Omkar Bhatt.

Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Chen earned a PhD at Yale University, studying under doctoral supervisors Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff, as well as teacher Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Ra completed doctoral studies at Temple University under supervisor Charles Wei-hsun Fu and teachers Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Langdon Warner (1881–1955) was a scholar of history, archaeology, sinology, and japanology who earned an A.B. from Harvard University. He directed the Philadelphia Museum of Art and held posts at the Fogg Art Museum and Harvard, among other museums.

Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned a PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes. She serves as Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism at McGill (attested 2026).

Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota. He taught at Minnesota, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the University of Washington, and was attested at Langara College in 2005.

Lars Edman (1824–1921) was a Swedish scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned his fil.kand. (Ph.D.) at Uppsala University, where he served as Docent in Oriental languages in 1857 and as Associate Professor of German and English from 1863 to 1892.

Lars Fogelin is an archaeologist, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD under Carla Sinopoli at the University of Michigan in 2003. He has held positions at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse (b. 1950) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oslo, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn. He was attested as a teacher at the University of Oslo in 2002.

Lars Nannestad Boisen (1803–1875) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Bonn, learning under Georg Freytag, August Wilhelm von Schlegel, Christian Lassen, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard Chézy.

Lata Chhatre is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. She held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University as Reader in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2009) and as Visiting Faculty (attested 2026).

Lata Deokar is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who completed an MA and PhD at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth. She worked on a dictionary at CIHTS (2000–2012) and was attested at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 2026.

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Ganden Shartse and Gyuto Monasteries. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (~1976–1985) and was a Visiting Scholar at the University of Virginia in 1976.
Latika Lahiri (b. 1923) is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji in 1958. She later held a post at the University of Delhi.

Laura Harrington is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who studied at Columbia University. Her teachers included Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., Gary A. Tubb, Lobsang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, Tenzin Norbu, Nathaniel Dickson, and Gregory Hillis.

Laura Massetti is a linguist and Indologist who earned a PhD at the University of Cologne in 2016. She held posts at Copenhagen, Oxford, the Center for Hellenic Studies, and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2022–2025).

Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetologist who held posts at Indiana University Bloomington, Latse Library, and Rutgers. Attested at Columbia University in 2026, she has served as Adjunct Assistant Professor in Tibetan Literature and Director of the Modern Tibetan Studies Program.

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who studied medicine at the University of Glasgow. He was Professor of Chemistry and Pathology at Calcutta Medical College and Professor of Tibetan at University College London.

Laurence Binyon (1869–1943) was an art historian, sinologist, and japanologist educated at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Keeper of Oriental Prints and Drawings at the British Museum and held visiting professorships at Harvard University and the University of Athens.

Laurence Khantipalo Mills (1932–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under teachers including Acharya Buddharakkhita, Sangharakshita, Chien Ming Chen, Dhardo Rinpoche, Namkhai Norbu, and Dudjom Rinpoche. He served as abbot at Wat Buddha Dhamma in 1978.
